title: Under the Veil
subtitle: The bullet spares neither the kind nor the cruel; all are caught in the same tragic fate.

content.text: Look at these boys. They left home with puffed chests and confident smiles on their faces—
Thinking they'd go to the front, pull a few triggers, kill a few enemies, and come back as heroes.
But when their feet hit the soil, they turned "pacifist," it seems, wounding their own hands rather than their enemies'.
Their mothers should have begged them to stay, not waved their handkerchiefs to see them off.

branch.text: Soldiers follow orders, officers give them, higher-ups make them, parents send their children off to die ...
And not one of them will bear the weight of their "misjudgments." Only the dead must answer.
Really? You think death is the only option?
What could possibly be the point in that?
Don't tell me you believe there's GLORY in dying on the battlefield? The thought makes me sick.
Look there—at the lifeless body lying flat in the mud.
He couldn't even muster the courage to flee, so he bribed a fellow soldier—a man he barely knew—with three cigarettes to surrender with him.
He died—killed in a moment of pure, senseless hatred. And the other lived—saved by a flicker of mercy.
Where should his mother aim her grief? At the officer who changed his mind just a moment too late? Hah!
The officer will be pardoned; they'll say he, too, was a victim of this endless, miserable cycle of hatred.
So tell me—please, tell me—to whom this rage should go, and I will take this kitchen knife and plunge it into their heart!

items.text: Under the Veil

"In the first three months, I had no idea who I was fighting or what lay on the other side of the trenches. 
It was as if there were a black wall standing between us and our enemy."
"They could attack at any time. I can't sleep. I don't want to die. I don't want to see their faces. I don't want to know what our enemy looks like. And worst of all, I don't know why."

By the time Charon returns to the trenches, the most recent bombardment has already ended. A trench can never really be called calm, but the rattle of machine guns and the crack of rifles slow and fade into the background.
The shelling hasn't changed much—a few new craters to replace the old ones.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Ah so, you're back, mailman. Tell us, where did you take little Franz?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He lies beneath stone in a silent wood and marches no more.
Erich grunts out a reply. He's standing in Franz's boots—freshly shined.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Hmph. I bet Mr. Willi you'd take the opportunity to keep walking and never come back. Lucky me.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Where is he?

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: He's dead. I guess you'll call me "Mr. Captain" now.
Erich casts his eyes to a new crater decorating their trench.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: He caught a shell. Just like that.
Erich's face pales and then runs flush red, throbbing veins straining out along his forehead.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Lucky me. Unlucky him. That bastard!
He rushes to Charon, grabbing him by the collar.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: He died, and now who do I pay up to? Why'd you even bother coming back? We have enough ghosts in this goddamn trench!
Erich pulls Charon up and tosses him against the trench wall.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: You waltz through here whenever you like just to take away our brothers. You bury them. Why? Why do you get to return and they stay dead? Are you mocking us?
Charon slumps but does not fall, making no effort to fight against Erich's strength.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Death does not mock. Nor can it stop its return. It is as helpless as any other soldier to do his duty.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What fate lies ahead of us is unknown; its winding path cannot be seen until we step through it. None choose the hour when death finds us.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: S**t!
A curse, flat and empty, and just like that, the fire and fury are gone from him.
Soldiers walk by, look away, and continue their work. A hundred pairs of eyes, and each of them numb to the chaotic scene.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: I just want to keep myself in one piece when my time comes. Better make sure I look good for my funeral, alright? Now, off you go.

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: Sir, there's movement coming from no man's land.
The spotter interrupts their standoff, handing Erich a trench periscope.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: What?
Erich grabs the scope and crouches up to a nearby parapet.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Hmm, that's just two soldiers. Could it be a trench raid?

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: I don't think so, Mr. Captain. Why would they go over the top in broad daylight? Look, they're waving their arms.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Huh? What are they doing? Wait, their hands are wrapped in bandages.

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: Is that a problem?
Erich returns the periscope to the spotter.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Keep your eye on them, soldier. I think I know what's going on.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The living walk over dead men's ground.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Deserters, I'll bet. I heard some soldiers used to shoot their own palms so they could be sent back to the rear. But they reward that kind of cowardice with bullets nowadays.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Do they come seeking death or life?

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: With all the officers keeping their heads low, maybe they decided they don't want to do the punishing themselves? Just kick these poor bastards out of the trench and tell them to walk till they drop.
Old and new memories intertwine in Charon's mind, forming an incomplete but certain thought.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: They do not march to us as warriors but as broken men.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: You're right. Pass it down the line. Does anyone here speak French?

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: Yes. A little. I took some French back in school.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Hurry, hurry! Say something!

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: Yes, Mr. Captain.
The spotter presses his head against the sandbags, trying to project his voice through the firing slit.

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: Hey, you, over there!

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: Let go of your—er—weapons and ... ah—just come here!

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: We ...

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: What the ...!

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Goddamn! Who the hell shot him?
Voices carry from around the trench line.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: What are you waiting for, soldier?
The major's face is ashen and stiff.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: I killed him.
Rudolph stammers out the words, lying propped up against a sandbag, wisps of gray smoke lingering out from his shaking rifle.
His glasses are thick as a church window, and still he's the best marksman in the company.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: And the other bastard's still standing! Are you blind?

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: But Mr. Major, he's surrendered. He ... dropped his weapon.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: It's a trap, you idiot! They have a bomb or some kind of infectious disease!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Do you want to keep him, soldier? You going to share your rations with him?

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Mr. Major, we're supposed to accept all prisoners. There are camps to send them to ... or even the safe zone.
He pulls his pistol and points it at the marksman's chest.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: That was an order, soldier. You are to shoot that foreign devil, or I'll send you out to test if their snipers are as spineless as you are.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Major.
Rasping voices ripple down the trench as bodies make way for a figure moving like a charge in slow motion.
Major Braun turns toward the sound.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Charon? What took you so long? Don't you know I could have you shot for dereliction of duty?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Punish the guilty then, but the man that stands alone is innocent. Spare him.
The statement is stunning in its sharpness. Defiance is not a trait Major Braun has come to expect from him.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: You are not entitled to challenge my authority, sergeant.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: His war is over. His blood should not water these fields.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Cowards!
Major Braun strides forward in a single step, boots thudding against the trench's wooden planks.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Bastard!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: You're just like those foreigners, poisoning the hearts of our youth with feckless sentimentality—your weakness, this fatalism—is a plague spreading through our ranks!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: That man over there is a threat to our fatherland, yet you plead for his life!
A single unblinking stare sweeps over the gathered soldiers, cowing each man into silence.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: I won't let this cowardice ruin our nation! We will keep fighting until no man alive stands against us! Only through their blood and our tireless sacrifice will we grow fearless and retrieve the glory of our birthright!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There is no glory for the dead, Eberhard. Only suffering, guilt, and regret for those that remain.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No courage is found in the blood of the innocent, only stains that can never be washed out.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Nonsense!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I remember, you, Major Braun, my old friend, would never say these things.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What lies were whispered in your ears by Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Shut up! That's slander! Who told you that?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I ... do not slander you, Mr. Major.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Explain yourself. Explain all of this!
The man roars, and for a second time, Charon is slammed against the trench wall.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Lies—Manus Vindictae—what do you mean?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: These are not your eyes.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Answer me!
But this man's fire does not temper. It bursts.
Charon reacts too slowly to evade the pistol as it is smashed across his head.
Major Braun's eyes are fixed on the pistol in his hand, anger replaced with shock.
Charon, now wounded, raises his hand to meet his bowed head. Beneath the "curtain," something seems to crack.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Raise your head, sergeant.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Eberhard ...

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Do not call me that! I am your superior officer. Damn! Obey my orders!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It should not have been this way.
He raises his head. The movement is heavy and labored.
A hollow and foreboding presence seems to fill the trench around them.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Good heavens ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: This is not a sight fit for the living, Eberhard.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But perhaps you must be reminded.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: No! Your face. Cover it now!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Do you remember the fear as bombs exploded by our sides, the pain when our brothers moaned out their last breaths? Have you forgotten, or have you only hardened your heart?

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: This war is ... *cough* sacrifice is necessary for a nation to make progress.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Every soldier who has died for the fatherland should feel honored for their sacrifice! You should have been honored, Paul—

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: We do not speak of sacrifice now.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Death is not honored—death knows no ceremony, it holds no virtues, it is emptiness and void.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You have become so numb to death that you laugh as it walks among us. It is so close to you that you have mistaken it for life, Eberhard.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There is nothing to be gained from this war that will pay for what we have already lost.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: You ... want me dead ... then kill me ... do it.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Death will not save you, old friend.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I want you to save yourself.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: I ... Ugh ...
The other soldiers huddle to the side.
Major Braun collapses to the ground. His eyes swirl and then go blank, looking up and nowhere at the same time. His face is bone white and stiff as a corpse.
Charon kneels over him and closes his eyes. A motion all too familiar to those watching.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: S**t! What the hell just happened?
Rudolph peeks out from the crowd, managing a question both timid and brave.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Is Major Braun dead? Charon, you didn't ...

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Did you?
Charon stands, deliberately facing away from the crowd, replacing his mask and hood with careful precision.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He will live. We will leave here together.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You have command, Erich. Make the right choices.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I don't want you to see what lies beneath. Please, look away.
Words bulge at the edge of Erich's lips, but he swallows them back.
All others stand stunned and silent as Charon departs with Major Braun in tow.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: *tut*

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Alright. Someone grab that deserter. I'll search him.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Show's over. Move it, soldiers! That poor sap is still waiting. Get moving!
